name: Tawang Monastery (Gaden Namgyal Lhatse)
description: Largest Buddhist monastery in India and second-largest in the world, founded in 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso. Overlooks Tawang Chu valley with a 28-foot gilded Buddha, ancient manuscripts, and about 500 monks of the Gelug school. Birthplace region of the 6th Dalai Lama; major pilgrimage site.
facts: Founded 1680-81 by Merak Lama Lodre Gyatso
Houses 28-ft gilded Buddha and rare manuscripts

name: Bomdila
description: Headquarters of West Kameng district and a popular hill station on the Tezpur-Tawang highway at about 2,415 m elevation. Features apple orchards, Buddhist gompas, craft centres, and panoramic Himalayan views; key overnight stop on the western Arunachal circuit.
facts: Home to GRL Monastery and apple orchards

name: Bomdila Monastery (Gontse Gaden Rabgyel Ling / GRL)
description: Prominent Gelugpa Buddhist monastery above Bomdila town, also known as Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Ling. Offers sweeping valley views, active monastic life, and traditional Tibetan architecture; a major spiritual and cultural landmark of West Kameng.
facts: Also known as GRL or Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Ling
Features prayer halls and resident monks

name: Dirang
description: Scenic valley town in West Kameng known for its Dzong (old fort), hot springs, apple orchards, and proximity to Sangti Valley and Mandala Top. Serves as a base for exploring Monpa culture and Himalayan landscapes.
facts: Known for Dirang Dzong and hot springs
Gateway to Sangti Valley and Mandala Top

name: Sangti Valley
description: Picturesque valley about 14 km from Dirang, surrounded by Eastern Himalayan ranges. Famous for black-necked cranes in winter, terraced fields, and serene river landscapes; a hidden gem for nature and bird lovers.

name: Thembang Fortified Village (Thembang Dzong)
description: Ancient Monpa fortified village and Dzong on UNESCO’s tentative World Heritage list. Features traditional stone-and-wood architecture, two historic gates, and a living cultural landscape at about 2,169–2,300 m elevation.
facts: Traditional Monpa architecture with two gates

name: Eaglenest Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area in the Himalayan foothills of West Kameng, renowned for exceptional bird diversity including the Bugun liocichla. Elevations range from 500 to 3,250 m; part of the Kameng Elephant Reserve and conjoins Sessa Orchid Sanctuary.
facts: Home to Bugun liocichla and rich avifauna
Part of Kameng Protected Area Complex

name: Sessa Orchid Sanctuary
description: 100 km² orchid-focused sanctuary in West Kameng, established in 1989. Protects over 200 orchid species in subtropical to temperate forests; linked to the Orchid Research Centre at Tippi and conjoins Eaglenest WLS.

name: Tippi Orchid Research Centre
description: Major orchid research and conservation centre near Bhalukpong on the banks of the Bharali/Kameng river. Houses thousands of orchid specimens, glasshouses, and a museum; gateway attraction for the western Arunachal circuit.

name: Nyukmadong War Memorial
description: Memorial near Dirang honouring Indian soldiers who fell in the 1962 Indo-China war. Features a 25-foot chorten-style memorial on terraced grounds with plaques listing names; a solemn site overlooking the battlefield.
facts: Located near Dirang on Bomdila-Tawang road

name: Bhalukpong
description: Gateway town at the Arunachal Pradesh–Assam border on the Kameng/Bharali river. Entry point for the western circuit, known for river picnic spots, orchid centre proximity, and historical ruins.
facts: Southern entry to West Kameng from Assam

name: Mandala Top (108 Manes / Stupas)
description: Hilltop site near Dirang featuring a circular arrangement of 108 Buddhist stupas (manes) built in 2018, each inscribed with Om Mani Padme Hum. Offers panoramic Himalayan views and is a popular birdwatching spot.
facts: 108 stupas built in 2018 by local community

name: Chillipam Monastery (Sangngag Choekhor Dargyeling)
description: Nyingma monastery near Rupa village in West Kameng, perched on a promontory with 270-degree views. Established in the early 20th century; an important centre of Tibetan Buddhism in the district.

name: Lhagyala Gompa
description: Historic 17th-century monastery at Morshing, overlooking the Morshing valley. An important Monpa spiritual site about 80 km from Bomdila.

name: Shergaon
description: Remote village and area in West Kameng known for horticulture farms, apple cultivation, and proximity to wildlife habitats. Offers quiet offbeat stays and access to surrounding forests.
facts: Part of western circuit off main highway

name: Dirang Hot Springs
description: Natural hot springs near Dirang town, popular for relaxation amid the valley setting. A traditional local attraction on the Bomdila-Tawang route.
facts: Popular stop for travellers on NH13
